Key responsibilities include: collaborating with project teams to solve real-world client problems within federal missions; translating business and mission objectives into technology-driven strategies and solutions; experimenting with emerging technologies including agentic AI and modern development tools; applying structured thinking, creativity, and analysis to develop recommendations; contributing to software engineering, data analysis, or technology advisory tasks depending on project alignment; participating in learning experiences, mentorship opportunities, workshops, and networking; and supporting digital transformation efforts through research, testing, documentation, and solution design.

Qualifications: must be a rising senior (4th-year undergraduate) with graduation by August 31, 2028; GPA 3.2+ from a 4-year accredited institution; U.S. citizenship required; ability to travel 25–50% preferred. Preferred majors include Computer Science, Information Systems, IT, Engineering, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Business, Economics, Public Policy, Liberal Arts, or STEM with demonstrated interest in data analytics, information systems, or coding.

item.title: Young Professionals Programme (YPP) – Development & Sustainability
item.description:
Application period: October–November 2026. Apply via inspira.un.org. The 2026 application window is now open.

Note: This is a competitive examination program, not a direct hire. Successful candidates are placed on a roster for P-1 or P-2 level positions — placement on the roster does not guarantee an offer of employment. For 2026, the United States is a participating country for the Development and Sustainability exam area only. Must be 32 years of age or younger (born on or after January 1, 1994). Must be willing to serve at any UN duty station worldwide. Attach a government-issued photo ID and degree documentation to your application.

The UN Young Professionals Programme (YPP) is a recruitment initiative for talented professionals to start a career as an international civil servant with the UN Secretariat. The examination process consists of a two-stage online written exam followed by a competency-based video-conference interview. Successful candidates are placed on a roster valid for three years from which they are selected to fill appropriate vacancies at UN offices worldwide (including Addis Ababa, Bangkok, Beirut, Geneva, Nairobi, New York, Santiago, and Vienna). Successful candidates receive a two-year fixed-term contract at the P-1 or P-2 level, with the possibility of a continuing contract after two years subject to satisfactory performance.

Estimated timeline: Application period October–November → Applications screened December–January → Assessment process February–May → Interviews and results June–August. Note: timeline varies year to year.

The YPP exam has two online stages: Stage 1 consists of approximately 2 hours of multiple choice questions (general and specialized), available in English or French. Stage 2 consists of approximately 2–2.5 hours of specialized constructed-response questions; may be proctored remotely. Candidates successful in both stages are invited to a competency-based video-conference interview.

Eligibility requirements: nationality of a participating Member State (U.S. eligible for Development & Sustainability exam area in 2026); a bachelor's degree or equivalent (at least a 3-year degree) relevant to the exam area; 32 years of age or younger in 2026 (born on or after January 1, 1994); fluency in English or French (UN Level II proficiency required in all four areas — speaking, reading, writing, and understanding).

Compensation and logistics: P-1 or P-2 level UN salary scale (competitive international civil service compensation including benefits and allowances — confirm current rates via careers.un.org). 2-year fixed-term contract. Placement at any UN duty station worldwide. Application via inspira.un.org. Application period: October–November 2026.
